sources.citation: De Vries, James A. & Sandra A. De Vries. 1997. An overview of Kwerba verb morphology. In Andrew Pawley (ed.), Papers in Papuan linguistics No. 3 (Pacific Linguistics A-87), 1-35. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing on Airoran. For Kwerba itself no word-stress rule either; the only prosodic words are about the pre-verbal transitional syllable: 'Ra is a weakly stressed syllable attaching itself as a postclitic to the word preceding the verb.. when the preceding word ends with an unstressed syllable, the ra tends to be absorbed and is not pronounced' (sec. 2, p. 4).

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane; Mark Donohue; Felix Ma. 2002. Survey report of the north coast of Irian Jaya. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-078. Dallas: SIL International. 10 pp. (downloaded from Internet Archive copy of www-01.sil.org/silesr/2002/)
sources.note: Sec. 4.3 'Airoran and Samarokena' (printed p. 9, p. 8) gives a tentative phoneme chart, notes an s/h contrast and a seven-vowel system, and remarks only: 'There are also some instances of a stressed schwa appearing in the data, suggesting that schwa might also be a contrastive sound'. No statement of where stress falls; authors say 'very little of their structure was discovered'.

sources.citation: Google Books legacy feed queries '"Airoran" stress/phonology/accent/tone/syllable/language' (saved:) and archive.org advancedsearch 'Airoran'
sources.note: '"Airoran" stress' = 0 hits; other queries return only classification/overview mentions (Wurm 1975, Voorhoeve 1975 checklist, Galis 1956, Silzer & Clouse 1991 index, encyclopedias, Donohue 1999 Warembori). archive.org holds only Wikipedia-article PDFs. No source describing Airoran prosody surfaced.

sources.note: Phonology section reads '[under construction]'. Source census: all known Airoran materials are vocabularies (Anon. 1913 in Stokhof 1983: 47-50; Smits & Voorhoeve 1998: 22-233 'after van der Leeden'; SIL survey vocabularies) plus Clouse et al. 2002 phonemic inventory and pronouns. 'Nothing is known about Airoran verbal morphology.'

Section 1 'General information' gives list number, NBG 1913 mention, location, the Kwerba-family similarity remark and one transcription note: 'For typographic reasons the glottal stop in word-final position has been indicated by " e.g. 41: merna"'. Section 2 is the bare numbered Holle list (items 2-1423), section 3 'Notes' three glosses. No stress or length marks in the forms.
